lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ),
    let μ := (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))⁻¹
    Measurable γ ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure (νpos.bind γ) ∧
      IsProbabilityMeasure (νneg.bind γ) ∧
      (∀ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), MeasurableSet B →
        (νpos.bind γ) B = ∫⁻ O, γ O B ∂νpos) ∧
      (∀ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), MeasurableSet B →
        (νneg.bind γ) B = ∫⁻ O, γ O B ∂νneg)
approved_definition_context: The measure is the canonical Borel probability on the full real orthogonal matrix group, obtained by normalizing Haar on the whole compact group. Both determinant signs are retained.

multivariateGaussian is the existing centered Gaussian probability constructor with the displayed inverse matrix as covariance. EuclideanSpace carries the genuine real Euclidean Borel structure. Measure spaces carry the sigma algebra generated by Borel-set evaluations.

For measures, restriction and scaling are literal. Measure.bind ν γ is Measure.join (Measure.map γ ν), the actual mixture. Measurable γ is proved as a conclusion, ensuring this is a genuine measurable mixture rather than a nonmeasurable-map fallback. IsProbabilityMeasure means total mass one.

The two source parameter inequalities are the only non-typing inputs. The Borel condition on B lies under universal quantification in the event-evaluation conclusions. No Gaussian-family, density, kernel, probability-prior or normalization producer result is a caller premise.
